405:
** ἀνδραποδ-ιστής**, οῦ, ὁ,
**slave-dealer** or **kidnapper,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 1030, “Pl.” 521, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 10.10, etc., compare 2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 3.78}}; coupled with ἱερόσυλοι, τοιχωρύχοι, etc., {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 344b: _metaphorically_, ἀ. ἑαυτοῦ}} **one who sells** his own **independence,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 1.2.6.}}
406:
**Ἀνδρέας**, -ου, ὁ
**Andrew, the Apostle**: Mat.4:18 10:2, Mrk.1:16, 29 3:18 13:3, Luk.6:14, Jhn.1:41, 45 6:8 12:22, Act.1:13.†
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
408:
**Ἀνδρόνικος**, -ου, ὁ
**Andronicus**: Rom.16:7.†
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
411:
** ἀνεκ-διήγητος**, ον,
**indescribable, ineffable,** {{NT+5th c.AD+|NT.2Cor.9.15, 5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus, variant in Aristeas 99.}}
415:
** ἀνελεήμων**, ον,
_genitive_ ονος, **merciless, without mercy,** {{NT+4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rh. Al.” 1442a13, NT.Rom.1.31, “Catalogus Codicum Astrologorum” 2.173}}:—also ἀνηλεήμων, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Nicochares Comicus 20; and in “Anecdota Graeca - Bekker” 400}} ἀνελήμων. _adverb_ ἀνελεημόνως, ἀπολέσθαι{{LXX+5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 1.25, LXX.Job.6.21.}}
416:
** ἀνεμ-ίζομαι**,
_passive_, **to be driven with the wind,** {{NT+8th c.BC+|NT.Jam.1.6, Scholia 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.336}}: _active_ in [{{Refs 5th c.AD+|5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus see at {ἀναψῦξαι}.}}]
418:
** ἀνέν-δεκτος**, ον,
**inadmissible, impossible,** {{NT+2nd c.AD+|NT.Luke.17.1, 2nd c.AD: Artemidorus Daldianus Onirocriticus 2.70.}}
419:
** ἀνεξ-ερεύνητος**
(Hellenistic ἀνεξεραύν-), ον, **not to be searched out,** {{NT+1st c.AD+|1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 18, NT.Rom.11.33, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 69.14.}}
420:
** ἀνεξῐκᾰκ-ος**, ον,
**enduring pain** or **evil,** {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st c.AD: Herodotus Medicus cited in 4th c.AD: Oribasius Medicus 5.30.7, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Jud.Voc.” 9, Vett. Val. 38.21, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 5.38, 4th c.AD: Themistius Sophista “Orationes” 15.190a (_superlative_), 2nd c.AD: Aretaeus Medicus “περὶ αἰτιῶν καὶ σημείων ὀξέων παθῶν” 2.6 (_comparative_)}}; **forbearing, long-suffering,** {{NT|NT.2Tim.2.24}}. _adverb_ **-κως**{{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Asin.” 2.}}
422:
** ἀνεπ-αίσχυντος**, ον,
**having no cause for shame,** {{NT+1st c.AD+|NT.2Tim.2.15; μηδὲ -τον ἡγοῦ 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 18.7.1.}}
423:
** ἀνεπί-ληπτος**, ον,
**not open to attack,** τοῖς ἐχθροῖς{{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.17}}; **not censured, blameless,** βίος variant in {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 922, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.2.15}}; **perfect,** τέχνη{{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.15}}; ἀνεπιληπτότερον **less open to criticism,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 43c}}; ἐξουσία ἀ. **not subject to control,** {{Refs 1st c.BC+|1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 2.14}}; **unassailable, not subject to cancellation,** συγγραφαί{{Refs|“PTaur.” 1.7.15}}. _adverb_ **-τως**{{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.6.37, 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 2.2, +others}}
428:
** ἀνεύθετος**, ον,
**inconvenient,** λιμὴν ἀ. πρὸς παραχειμασίαν{{NT|NT.Act.27.12.}}
431:
** ἀνεψι-ός**, ὁ,
**first cousin,** or generally, **cousin,** [{{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.464, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.30, 7.82, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 856, “Comica Adespota” 58D., etc., see especially 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.47; ἀ. πρὸς πατρός 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 11.2; ἐκ πατρός 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 22.170: comically, ἐγχέλεων ἀ. 5th c.BC: Strattis Comicus 39. [ἀνεψιοῦ κταμένοιο 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.554, ={ἀνεψιόο κτ}.,compare 4th c.AD(?): Quintus Smyrnaeus Epicus 3.295}}].] (Cf. Sanskrit ναπᾱτ 'grandson', Latin _nepos,_ etc.)
432:
** ἄνηθον**
or ἄννηθον, τό, _Aeolic dialect_ ἄνητον {{Refs 7th c.BC+|7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 36, 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 78,128, also 6th c.BC: Anacreon Lyricus cited in 2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 6.107. ἄννητον 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 9.7.3}}:— **dill, Anethum graveolens,** {{NT+5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 982, “Th.” 486, 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 1.11.2, 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 127.5, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 15.119, NT.Matt.23.23, 1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 3.58, “SIG” 1170.26 (2nd c.AD), Bilabel Ὀψαρτ. p.10. (ἀνν- in Ar.[same places] Not to be confused with ἄννησον, which see)}}
434:
** ἀνήμερ-ος**, ον,
**not tame, wild, savage,** of persons, πολιήτας{{NT+6th c.BC+|6th c.BC: Anacreon Lyricus 1.7; ἀνήμεροι γάρ, οὐδὲ πρόσπλατοι ξένοις 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 716, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Carneiscus Philosophus “Herc.” 1027.16, NT.2Tim.3.3, 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 1.3.7}}; of a country, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 14; ἐκβολή 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 1078; βίος 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.86d; διάθεσις 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Ir.” p.57}} W., compare p.85: _superlative_, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th-3rd c.BC: Clearchus Historicus 37}}. _adverb_ -ρως, ἀ. τισὶ χρήσασθαι{{Refs 1st c.BC+|1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 13.23.}}
445:
** ἀνθῠπᾰτ-εύω**,
**to be proconsul,** {{NT+1st c.AD+|1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Comp. Dem.Cic.” 3, NT.Act.18.12, 2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus 7.5.2.}}
448:
** ἀνίλεως** [ῑ], ων,
_Attic dialect_ for ἀνίλαος (not in use), **unmerciful,** {{NT+2nd c.AD+|NT.Jam.2.13 (assuming variant), 2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus “Epim.” 257.}}
451:
**Ἄννα**, -ας, ἡ (Heb. חָנָה),
**Anna, a prophetess**: Luk.2:36.†
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
452:
**Ἄννας**, -α (FlJ, Ἄνανος, -ου), ὁ (Heb. חָנַן),
**Annas, the high priest**: Luk.3:2, Jhn.18:13-24, Act.4:6.†
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
454:
** ἄνοια**,
_Epic dialect_ ἀνοίη {{Refs 6th c.BC+|6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 453}}, ἡ:— **the character of an** ἄνοος, **want of understanding, folly,** ἀνοίη **in folly,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.69; ὑπ᾽ ἀνοίας 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 1079, 4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 143; νεότητι καὶ ἀνοία 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 716a; ἄ. λόγου 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 603; τὴν ἄ. εὖ φέρειν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 398}}; πολλῆ ἀνοια χρῆσθαι to be **a** great **fool,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 3.3.2; πολλὴ ἄ. [ἐστι] πολεμῆσαι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.61}}; ἄνοιαν ὀφλισκάνειν to be thought **a fool,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 1.26; δύο ἀνοίας γένη, τὸ μὲν μανίαν, τὸ δ᾽ ἀμαθίαν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 86b}}; but opposed to μανία, {{Refs|[prev. author] “R.” 382c, 382e, etc.}}: _plural_, **follies,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 8.7. [In Trag. sometimes paroxyt. ἀνοίᾱ (compare ἀγνοίᾱ),compare 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 402, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 583.5, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 519.]}}
457:
** ἄνοιξις**, εως, ἡ,
**opening,** πυλῶν{{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.67, 68; πόρων 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Odoribus” 13; χειλῶν 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.738c, compare “PMag.Lond.” 46.274 (4th c.AD): _plural_, 3rd c.AD: Porphyrius Tyrius Philosophus “de Antro Nympharum - Porphyrii Opuscula” 27}}; ἄ. τοῦ στόματος, Hebraism for παρρησία, {{LXX+NT|LXX.Eze.29.21, NT.2Cor.6.11, NT.Eph.6.19, etc.}}
465:
** ἀντάλλᾰγ-μα**, ατος, τό,
**that which is given** or **taken in exchange,** φίλου **for** a friend, {{NT+5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 1157, cf. LXX.Job.28.15, +others; τῆς ψυχῆς NT.Matt.16.26, compare 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus “Fragmenta” 110H.}}
466:
** ἀντανα-πληρόω**,
**fill up,** τὴν θέσιν τοῦ ὀνόματος{{NT+2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Syntaxi;” 14.1; τὰ ὑστερήματα τῶν θλίψεων τοῦ Χριστοῦ NT.Col.1.24}}; ἀ. πρὸς τὸν εὐπορώτατον ἀεὶ τοὺς ἀπορωτάτους **put in** the poorest **so as to balance** the richest, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 14.17.}}
468:
** ἀνταπό-δομα**, ατος, τό,
**repayment, requital,** whether of good or evil, {{LXX+NT|LXX.Sir.12.2, 14.6, +others, NT.Luke.14.12, NT.Rom.11.9.}}
475:
** ἀντιδια-τίθημι**,
**retaliate upon** a person, {{Refs 1st c.BC+|1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 34.12; κακῶς παθόντα ἀ 12th c.AD: Eustathius Episcopus Thessalonicensis 546.28}}:—_middle_, **offer resistance,** πρὸς τὴν πειθώ{{Refs 3rd c.AD+|3rd c.AD: Longinus Rhetor 17.1; τοὺς ἀντιδιατιθεμένους}}**opponents,** {{NT|NT.2Tim.2.25.}}
476:
** ἀντίδῐκ-ος**, ον,
**opponent** or **adversary in a suit,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.165, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 273c: _feminine_, ἡ ἀ. “POxy.” 37i8(1st c.AD)}}: properly, **the defendant,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 1.2}}; but also, **the plaintiff,** Lys7.13; ἀ. πρός τινα{{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 1.5}}:—generally, **opponent, adversary,** {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 41}}; ἀληθινῶν ἀ. [{{NT+1st c.BC+|1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus] 133, cf. NT.1Pet.5.8, 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Ir.” p.65W.}}
479:
** ἀντικᾰλέω**,
**invite in turn,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 1.15(in}}_future_ _passive_ -κληθήσομαι),compare {{NT|NT.Luke.14.12.}}
481:
** ἀντικρύ**,
_adverb_ ={ἄντην}, **over against, right opposite,** θεοῖς ἀντικρὺ μάχεσθαι I 1.5.130: with _genitive_, Ἕκτορος ἀντικρύ [prev. work = 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica”] 8.301.
**II** ={ἄντῐκρυς}, **straight on, right on,** ἀντικρὺ δόρυ χάλκεον ἐξεπέρησεν{{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 10.162; ἀντικρὺ μεμαώς I 1.13.137}}: mostly followed by a _preposition_, ἀντικρὺ δ᾽ ἀν᾽ ὀδόντας{{Refs 8th c.BC+|5.74; ἀντικρὺ δι᾽ ὤμου 4.481, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.16}}; ἀντικρὺ κατὰ μέσσον **right** in the middle, {{Refs|I 1.16.285}}; once in {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus, ἀντικρὺ διᾴττων “Cyr.” 7.1.30}}; compare καταντῑκρύ.
**II.2** **outright, utterly, quite,** ἀντικρὺ δ᾽ ἀπόφημι{{Refs 3rd c.BC+|I 1.7.362; ἀντικρὺ δ᾽ ἀπάραξε 16.116; ἀντικρὺ μακάρεσσιν ἔϊκτο 3rd c.BC: Apollonius Rhodius Epicus 4.1612, etc. (Cf. ἄντικρυς entry near the end) [ν ¯ generally, but ῠ I 1.5.130, 819}}; ῐ by nature {{Refs 5th c.BC+|compare (καταντῐκού 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 87), ῑ by po ition in _Epic dialect_]}}
486:
** ἀντιλοιδορέω**,
**rail at** or **abuse in turn,** {{NT+3rd c.BC+|PPetr. 3p.48 (3rd c.BC), 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.88f (_passive_), NT.1Pet.2.23}}:—_middle_, with _accusative_ _of things_, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Symp.” 40.}}
490:
**Ἀντιόχεια**, -ας, ἡ
**Antioch**;
1. **in Syria**: Act.11:19-22, 26-27 13:1 14:26 15:22-23, 30 15:35 18:22, Gal.2:11
2. **In Pisidia**: Act.13:14 14:19, 21, 2Ti.3:11.†
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
491:
**Ἀντιοχεύς**, -έως, ὁ
**a citizen of Antioch, an Antiochian**: Act.6:5.†
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
493:
**Ἀντίπας** (T, Ἀντείπας), -α (in some MSS. it appears to be indecl.; but see M, Pro.12:1-28; it is abbrev. from Ἀντίπατρος), ὁ,
**Antipas**: Rev.2:13.†
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
494:
**Ἀντιπατρίς**, -ίδος, ἡ
Antipatris, bet. Joppa and Caesarea: Act.23:31.†
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
497:
** ἀντιστρᾰτεύομαι**,
**take the field, make war against,** τινί{{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 8.8.26}}:—later in _active_, {{Refs 1st c.BC+|1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 22.15, 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 2.10.1 (_absolutely_): _metaphorically_, Ἔρωτες ἀ. τοῖς ὑπερηφανοῦσι 5th c.AD: Aristaenetus Rhetor 2.1.}}
